paper.title: The calculation of e to many significant digits

program.how: written for ounce-core from the method (e = 2 + sum 1/i! held in factorial-base digits all equal to 1, repeated multiplication by 10 with carries propagated from position N down to 2); small-integer arithmetic only; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: with N = 3300 factorial-base positions the spigot produces 10000 digits of e (the 2 and 9999 decimals), all equal to the digits listed in OEIS A001113

expected_values_source.what: the decimal digits of e (sequence A001113), first 10000 digits, copied as data. Sale's article itself was not fetched; the method is the standard factorial-base spigot it describes.
expected_values_source.note: the digit list and the program are independent of each other

negative_control: built with -DSALE_N=3000 (3000! has only about 9130 digits, so too few positions), the first difference is at digit 9135, a difference is reported and the program exits 1
not_checked: more than 10000 digits, and Sale's own figures (not fetched)
the choice of N in general (the check uses N = 3300 chosen so that N! exceeds 10^10000 with margin)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, reproduces the first 10000 digits of e with the spigot method. It does not show anything about other digit counts.
